Jackson's Star Colony CanteenAlien: RomulusNo sun on Jackson's Star. Plenty of gravy.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersJackson's Star miners' pastiesCrimped shortcrust pasties of diced beef, potato, swede and onion with plenty of black pepperHow to make it350g beef skirt steak, finely diced1 potato, finely diced150g swede, finely diced1 onion, finely diced3 sheets of frozen shortcrust pastry, thawed20g butter1 egg, beatensalt and plenty of black pepper, to tasteDice the steak, potato, swede and onion small and evenly.Mix together and season hard with salt and pepper.Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut 4 large rounds from the pastry, pile the filling on one half of each, dot with the butter, fold over and crimp the edge.Brush with the egg, cut a small steam hole and bake for 15 minutes, then turn the oven down to 170°C and bake 30 minutes more.Rest before serving.Andy's corny corn frittersCrisp sweet corn and spring onion fritters with coriander, served with lime sour creamHow to make it3 corn cobs1 egg80ml full cream milk75g plain flour1 tsp baking powder2 spring onions, sliced1 bunch coriander, chopped4 tbsp vegetable oil125g sour cream1 limesalt and pepper, to tasteStand each cob on its end and cut off the kernels.Whisk the egg, milk, flour, baking powder and a good pinch of salt and pepper into a thick batter.Fold in the corn, spring onions and most of the coriander.Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry heaped spoonfuls for 3 minutes a side, in batches, until golden. Drain on paper towel.Mix the sour cream with the lime zest and juice, scatter the rest of the coriander over the fritters and serve.MainsJackson's Star never-sunrise beef and barley stewSlow-braised beef chuck with carrot, celery and pearl barley in a thick gravy, with crusty breadHow to make it800g beef chuck, diced2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp vegetable oil1 onion, diced2 carrots, diced2 celery sticks, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp tomato paste1.2 L beef stock2 bay leaves1 tsp dried thyme100g pearl barley, rinsed1 tbsp flat-leaf parsley, chopped1 crusty loafsalt and pepper, to tasteToss the beef in the flour with salt and pepper. Dice the onion, carrots and celery and crush the garlic.Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef well in batches. Lift out.Soften the onion, carrots, celery and garlic in the same pot.Stir in the tomato paste, return the beef, add the stock, bay leaves and thyme and simmer, covered, on low.Stir in the barley and simmer, uncovered, until the barley is tender and the gravy thick.Season, scatter with parsley and serve with torn crusty bread.Renaissance station chicken katsu curryHot food before they board the derelict stationHow to make it2 large chicken breasts100g plain flour2 eggs150g panko breadcrumbs200ml vegetable oil1 brown onion2 carrots2 tbsp mild curry powder500ml chicken stock1 tbsp soy sauce1 tbsp honey300g short grain rice1 Lebanese cucumber2 tbsp rice vinegarFry the chopped onion and carrots in 1 tbsp of the oil for 8 minutes, stir in 2 tbsp of the flour and the curry powder, then add the stock, soy and honey and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend smooth.Simmer the rice with 450ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.Slice the cucumber thinly and toss with the rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar.Slice each breast in half through the middle. Dip in the rest of the flour, then beaten egg, then panko.Shallow fry in the rest of the oil for 3 minutes a side until golden, then slice.Serve the chicken over rice with the curry sauce poured alongside and the cucumber.SweetsYvaga sunshine lemon drizzle cakeButtery lemon loaf soaked in a crunchy lemon sugar drizzle while it is still warmHow to make it175g butter, softened175g caster sugar, for the cake3 eggs3 lemons, 2 zested, all 3 juiced175g self-raising flour2 tbsp full cream milk100g caster sugar, for the drizzleHeat the oven to 180°C and line a loaf tin with baking paper.Beat the butter and cake sugar until pale and fluffy.Beat in the eggs one at a time with the zest of 2 lemons, then fold in the flour and milk.Spoon into the tin and bake until risen and a skewer comes out clean.Mix the juice of all 3 lemons with the drizzle sugar.Prick the hot cake all over with a skewer, pour over the drizzle and leave to cool in the tin.DrinksCryo bay frozen lime slushieLime syrup blended with ice into a slushie, topped with soda water and fresh mintHow to make it100g caster sugar125ml water4 limes, juiced3 cups ice250ml soda water, chilled4 sprigs of mintSimmer the sugar and water until dissolved.Cool the syrup completely.Blend the syrup, lime juice and ice until slushy.Pour into 4 glasses, top with soda water and add a mint sprig.
